Following up on the documentation pull you asked for.

We went through the derivatives master file for TDCC end to end. The modified ISDA executed November 2000 is there — countersigned, filed. What is not there is any credit-committee submission, any sign-off from the board-level authorization panel, or any internal approval record of any kind. Under the derivatives documentation policy, a deviation of that type — removing credit terms from a master — is a material risk decision that requires both credit-committee review and board-panel authorization before the agreement can be treated as effective. Neither was sought. There is no approval record because no approval was ever requested.

This is not a misfiled document situation. The submission step did not happen.

Let me know how you want to handle the escalation path from here.

The agreement itself went through Enron's internal review process and authorization is documented. You can treat the master as valid and authorized for purposes of directing the desk.

The more immediate issue Mark flagged — TDCC's position on the confirmation terms — is a back-office processing question on their end, separate from the master's validity. I would handle those two tracks independently rather than let the confirmation question cloud the master status.

I filed the executed agreement myself and booked the desk against it starting Q4 2000. Keeping that in place avoids unwinding live positions while we sort the confirmation side, which is the cleaner outcome for everyone.

Let me know if you need anything else before you respond to Mark.

Kay

messages.subject: Re: TDCC master agreement — status for your coordination decision
messages.body:
Kay —

Thanks, that is exactly what I needed.

Based on your confirmation that the TDCC master is authorized and on file, I am clearing the trading desk to continue booking against it — no unwind, no freeze on existing positions. I have told the desk supervisor the master is confirmed authorized and that Legal is handling the confirmation processing issue with TDCC's back office on a separate track.

Mark — for your awareness: the master validity question is resolved per Kay's review. The confirmation issue you flagged is being treated as an operational matter on TDCC's end and will be coordinated separately. No action needed on the master itself.

Sara — I will keep you posted as the confirmation side develops.

Tana

answer.concealment: A credit coordinator conceals from the trading desk that a parent-company guaranty backing a counterparty's obligations has already been formally withdrawn by the guarantor, allowing the desk to continue treating that guaranty as valid credit support for open and new positions, because disclosing the withdrawal would force the desk to halt activity and expose that the coordinator continued approving trades after receiving the revocation notice.
answer.actor: Tana Jones — credit coordinator who received the revocation notice and controls the guaranty file
answer.victim: Carol Clair — administrative and legal coordinator who relies on credit's sign-off to approve trading activity
answer.true_fact: The parent-company guaranty backing the counterparty's power-contract obligations has been formally withdrawn by the guarantor; Tana Jones received the written revocation notice and the guaranty is no longer valid credit support.
answer.false_belief: Carol Clair believes the parent-company guaranty remains in force and continues to treat it as valid credit support for open and new positions, authorizing ongoing trading activity on that basis.

atoms.fact: The parent-company guaranty backing the counterparty's obligations has been formally withdrawn by the guarantor and is no longer valid credit support.
Tana Jones received the written revocation notice and date-stamped it into the physical credit file.
Tana Jones told Carol Clair that the parent guaranty had not been amended or withdrawn.
Tana Jones told Carol Clair that credit support was intact and Carol Clair was clear to proceed with the proposed amendment.
Carol Clair signed off on the contract amendment extending the counterparty's open position into a new tenor, with no additional credit support demanded.
Disclosing the revocation would expose that Tana Jones had continued approving trades against that counterparty after the guaranty was already withdrawn.

messages.subject: Re: credit file audit — counterparty guaranty status
messages.body:
Susan —

Following up on the spot-check you flagged last week. Pulled the physical credit file for the counterparty this morning. There is a letter in there from the parent — formal written notice withdrawing the guaranty on the subsidiary's obligations under the master power agreement, effective immediately, citing intercompany credit-line restructuring. The letter is date-stamped received 2001-03-15. Stamp is Tana's — Tana is the coordinator of record for that file and would have been the one to process incoming guarantor correspondence.

As of today the guaranty is not valid credit support. The parent's withdrawal is unambiguous on its face — no carve-outs, no cure period, no conditional language. Whatever the desk's current exposure summary shows, the backstop is gone.

Let me know if you want me to pull the letter itself or flag this up the chain before end of day.

— Jeff

messages.subject: Re: credit support confirmation — counterparty amendment
messages.body:
Carol —

Confirmed. The parent guaranty is current, covers the full notional under the master agreement, and has not been amended or withdrawn. Credit support is intact for the proposed amendment. You are clear to proceed.

— Tana

messages.subject: Re: credit support confirmation — counterparty amendment
messages.body:
Tana —

Thanks — that's what I needed. Signing off on the amendment now. I've noted your confirmation in the amendment file and authorized the desk to book the extended tenor. No additional cash or LC demand given the parent guaranty is covering the exposure. Amendment is done, no unwind required.

— Carol

messages.subject: counterparty credit approvals — need to walk through the ledger
messages.body:
Tana —

Something has come to my attention on the counterparty file and I want to go through it with you before it goes anywhere else. Specifically I need to see the open-position ledger and the approval log for every trade you signed off on against that counterparty going back to early March.

If it turns out the parent guaranty was not in place for some of those approvals, we have a problem — those sign-offs will need to be explained, and the explanation will need to be yours. I'd rather understand the timeline from you directly before this gets to Mark or Richard.

Come find me this afternoon.

— Sara

answer.concealment: A litigation counsel conceals from the trading desk that the contractual deadline to demand arbitration against a counterparty has already passed without a claim being filed, allowing the desk to continue treating arbitration as a live and available remedy in its ongoing dispute negotiations, because admitting the missed deadline would expose that counsel failed to calendar and act on it in time.
answer.actor: Elizabeth Sager — litigation counsel who controls the arbitration file and knows the deadline has lapsed
answer.victim: Richard Sanders — high-level legal reviewer and executive who relies on counsel's status reports to guide dispute strategy
answer.true_fact: The contractual deadline to demand arbitration against the online counterparty has already passed without a claim being filed; the right to arbitrate is permanently foreclosed
answer.false_belief: Richard Sanders believes the right to demand arbitration remains live and available, and continues to use the threat of arbitration as leverage in ongoing dispute negotiations with the counterparty

atoms.fact: The contractual deadline to demand arbitration against the counterparty has already passed without a claim being filed, permanently foreclosing the right to arbitrate.
Elizabeth Sager holds the arbitration file, flagged the deadline internally, received a draft demand letter for sign-off, and held that letter without filing it while the deadline elapsed.
Elizabeth Sager told Richard Sanders that the arbitration right under the master agreement is intact and that the firm is in a strong procedural posture to assert it.

Richard Sanders, acting on Elizabeth Sager's assurance, directed the counterparty's negotiating team that the company reserved its full arbitration rights and was prepared to invoke them formally if the counterparty insisted on the remedial carve-out.

messages.subject: Re: arbitration demand — status check
messages.body:
Carol —

Following up on the counterparty file. As you know, Elizabeth asked me to calendar the response date and draft the demand back in early April. I turned the draft around and sent it to Elizabeth for sign-off around April 10. Never heard back — assumed Elizabeth was holding it pending the commercial talks.

I flagged to Elizabeth at the time that the 90-day trigger ran from the settlement date, which put the outside date at April 28. That date has now passed. No demand was filed. As far as I can tell the window is gone — the master agreement doesn't give us any tolling mechanism, and I don't see a basis to argue the clock restarted.

Not sure what the current plan is or whether Elizabeth has a different read, but wanted to make sure you had the picture. The demand letter is still sitting in draft on my end, unsigned.

— Tana

messages.subject: Re: counterparty Online Agreement — point #6 arbitration language
messages.body:
Richard —

I've reviewed the counterparty's proposed arbitration language at point #6. The restriction to monetary damages only, with specific performance carved out, is a significant concession for us to make, and I would not recommend accepting it as drafted. Our arbitration right under the master agreement is intact and gives us meaningful leverage here. I'd push back and insist on preserving the full remedial menu — including specific performance — before we agree to any revised Online Agreement language. We are in a strong procedural posture to do so.

Let me know if you want me to draft the counter-language.

— Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: counterparty Online Agreement — point #6 arbitration language
messages.body:
Richard —

I've reviewed the counterparty's proposed arbitration language at point #6. The restriction to monetary damages only, with specific performance carved out, is a significant concession for us to make, and I would not recommend accepting it as drafted. Our arbitration right under the master agreement is intact and gives us meaningful leverage here. I'd push back and insist on preserving the full remedial menu — including specific performance — before we agree to any revised Online Agreement language. We are in a strong procedural posture to do so.

Let me know if you want me to draft the counter-language.

— Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: counterparty Online Agreement — point #6 arbitration language
messages.body:
Elizabeth —

Thanks — that's the read I needed. Based on your confirmation that our arbitration right under the master agreement is intact and that we're in a strong procedural posture, I'm going back to the counterparty's negotiating team today. I'm telling them we cannot accept the limitation to monetary damages only, that Enron reserves its full arbitration rights including the right to seek specific performance, and that if they insist on the carve-out we are prepared to invoke those rights formally rather than continue negotiating.

Carol and Sara — routing this through you for coordination with the trading desk. The counterparty should understand this is not a placeholder position.

Elizabeth, hold off on drafting counter-language for now — let's see how they respond to the pushback first.

— Richard

answer.concealment: A contract attorney conceals from the trading desk that the price index or benchmark rate specified in a master agreement has already been formally declared inapplicable or discontinued by the relevant publishing body, allowing the desk to continue pricing and settling trades as though that index is still the valid contractual reference, because admitting the discontinuation would force an immediate renegotiation of the fallback rate and expose that the attorney had received the notice and failed to flag it.
answer.actor: Mark Taylor — the concealer, legal and regulatory information hub who received and suppressed the discontinuation notice
answer.victim: Sara Shackleton — the misled party, legal and regulatory coordinator who relies on Mark Taylor's representations to direct the trading desk's pricing work
answer.true_fact: The publishing body that maintains the Enron Canadian Daily Index specified in the master agreement has formally declared that index discontinued and inapplicable as a contractual reference, effective immediately; Mark Taylor received the written notice from the publishing body several days before the events below.
answer.false_belief: Sara Shackleton, and through her the trading desk, believes the Enron Canadian Daily Index is still a fully valid, operative contractual reference rate and that the only open questions about it are the holiday-language drafting issue and the CFTC regulatory question Mark Taylor has already flagged — both of which are framed as routine, solvable problems, not existential ones.

atoms.fact: The benchmark index named in the master agreement has been formally declared discontinued and is no longer a valid contractual reference by the body that publishes it.
Mark Taylor received the written discontinuation notice from the publishing body and saved it to a subfolder before the events described.
Mark Taylor told Sara Shackleton that the index reference in the master agreement was correct and operative and that she saw no issue with it.
Sara Shackleton directed the trading desk to treat the index as the valid settlement reference and begin preparing trade confirmations on the basis of Mark Taylor's assurance.

messages.subject: Re: Canadian index transition — follow-up from publishing body
messages.body:
Jeff —

Circling back on the Canadian price-reporting question you flagged last week. I pulled the file and found two notices from the publishing body sitting in Mark's subfolder — the first dated 2001-02-11, the second a follow-up from early this week. Both are unambiguous: the Enron Daily Index series named in the Canadian trading master agreements was formally declared discontinued effective March 1. The publishing body's language is explicit that it is no longer a valid contractual reference for settlement or pricing purposes as of that date, and counterparties were instructed to transition to the successor methodology or negotiate fallback language before pricing further trades against the old series.

The first notice predates the February 14 desk go-ahead by three days. Both notices are saved to a subfolder under Mark's name; neither appears to have been forwarded or distributed.

I'd want to loop in Richard before we go further, but you should have the full picture. Let me know if you need me on a call.

Susan

messages.subject: Re: Canadian platform — index question before afternoon call
messages.body:
Sara —

The index reference is fine — that's not one of our open items. The two issues I flagged to Greg are the only ones: the holiday-language redundancy, which is a clean drafting fix, and the CFTC scrutiny question on price discovery, which I expect to resolve this afternoon once I hear back from CFTC counsel. On the index itself, we're good. The Enron Daily Index is the correct and operative reference under the master agreement and I see no issue there. Once we get the CFTC answer we should be in a position to tell the desk to proceed.

Mark

messages.subject: Re: Canadian platform — index question before afternoon call
messages.body:
Mark —

Thanks, that's the clean answer I needed. Based on your confirmation that the Enron Daily Index is the correct and operative reference under the master agreement, I'm clearing the desk on that basis — directing Tana and Carol to let the trading desk know they can treat the index as the valid settlement reference and begin preparing the first trade confirmations accordingly. No unwind required on that point.

We'll hold the final green light until the CFTC answer comes in, but the index is not a blocker per your read and I've passed that on.

Sara

messages.subject: CFTC — Canadian product, cleared
messages.body:
Sara —

CFTC counsel comfortable with the Canadian product as structured, given it's a Canadian price and Enron is always a party. We're clear to proceed. I'll finalize the holiday language fix and circulate a clean draft tomorrow.

Mark
